notes: This batch adds 86 person nodes and 82 person-to-person claims, reusing existing vp23_ripunjaya_mag at the chapter opening.
Parāśara presents chapter 24’s dynastic sequences as predictions. Claims preserve that framing and do not assert historical fact.

The chapter’s collective counts and unnamed members (including the seven unnamed sons of Mahāpadma and later dynastic groups) are not made into person nodes. Named persons appearing only in regional/group lists without a direct personal relationship are omitted rather than assigned unsupported links.

Repeated personal names receive chapter- and branch-specific IDs: Udayana · Śiśunāga branch is distinct from the Udayana in the earlier Parīkṣit branch; the two Nandivardhanas here are also separate; Śātakarṇi forms are separated when the passage introduces them as successive people.

ANU renders Mahāpadma or Nanda as a single ruler with alternative names; this batch uses one node rather than silently treating the names as two people. Kṛṣṇa in the Andhra succession is branch-tagged and is not merged with the deity or other namesakes.

Śipraka is called a minion of Suśarman and his brother Kṛṣṇa succeeds him; the source gives the brother relation directly. Parentage resumes with Kṛṣṇa’s son Śrīśātakarṇi. The displayed chain after that follows explicit “his son” wording.

Ripuṃjaya at 4.24.1 reuses the existing chapter 23 Magadha node. Devāpi’s chapter 24 Puru-line identification and Maru’s Ikṣvāku-family identification are named in 4.24.37; because Maru’s identity with any similarly named person in other batches is not explicit here, no identity merge is made.

The two unnamed rulers killed by Munika/Puṣpamitra and the unnamed mother of Mahāpadma are not assigned person nodes. Non-genealogical named regional/group catalogues are not converted into lineage assertions.

The passage also says Mahāpadma’s mother is śūdra, Pushpamitra kills an unnamed sovereign, Vasudeva is a Kaṇva, and Śipraka is of the Andhra clan. These are retained as textual observations here rather than person-to-person graph edges because the source does not name the other endpoint or it is a status/affiliation, not a person.
